elements.description: The overarching fraud objective or operation, typically composed of multiple tactics and techniques working together to achieve monetization or exploitation goals.
The high-level objectives or goals adversaries aim to achieve during a stage of a fraud scheme or operation.
The operational or transactional environments through which fraud activity is conducted, exploited, or targeted.
The specific methods, actions, or behaviors used by adversaries to execute a tactic or advance a fraud scheme.
Security controls, operational processes, or technologies designed to prevent, disrupt, or reduce the effectiveness of fraud techniques.
Telemetry, logs, behavioral indicators, or data sources that can be used to identify, investigate, or monitor fraud activity.
Supporting research, intelligence reporting, case studies, industry analysis, and other sources used to inform and validate taxonomy content.

schemes.description: Tampering, generating, stealing, or otherwise using a gift card in an unauthorized manner to extract resources.
Gaining unauthorized access to a victim's account
Deliberate exploitation of a return and refund policies to gain monetary value, store credit, gift cards, or replacement merchandise.

tactics.description: Operations that occur prior to compromise.
Stealing, generating, confirming, or otherwise obtaining a legitimate gift card, account, or other resource
Techniques that are used to bypass security measures and fraud controls
Physically or digitally gaining control of a resource from a customer or retailer
Converting illicitly gathered resources into liquid funds or an item that can be converted into liquid funds

techniques.name: Reconnaissance
techniques.description: Fraudsters actively or passively gather information that can be used to support operations. Information may include details of the victim organization, infrastructure, or staff/personnel. This information can be leveraged by the fraudster to aid in other phases of the adversary lifecycle, such as using gathered information to plan and execute future operations. Threat actors will attempt to create accounts, wish lists, and other related assets using lists of usernames and credentials from breached databases. If the attempt fails, it signals to the actor that the account already exists and is a good candidate for credential stuffing.

mitigations.name: Training and Awareness
mitigations.guidance: At physical locations, training employees to identify and report suspicious individuals to security.

mitigations.name: Security Guards
mitigations.guidance: At physical locations, use a security guard to identify and deter reconnaissance attempts.

mitigations.name: Software Configuration
mitigations.guidance: Fully decommission obsolete login software that may not be protected by current security protocols. Redirect login requests to obsolete software to follow the approved login flow.

detections.name: Network Traffic Attributes
detections.guidance: Automated network reconnaissance will scan internet resources in a manner that a normal user typically will not. Monitor for connections to suspicious ports and traversal to suspicious directories such as www.mywebsite.com/admin or www.mywebsite.com/phpadmin

detections.name: Online Identities
detections.guidance: When account creation has limited restrictions, fraudsters often create test accounts to develop automation, test fraud techniques, or validate stolen credentials. These accounts frequently use fake identity information and can provide insight into an actor’s methods and intent. Organizations should monitor account creation activity for abnormal behavior, as fraudsters may also use registration flows to determine whether accounts already exist before attempting credential-based attacks.

detections.name: Video Surveillance Systems
detections.guidance: At physical locations, use video surveillance to identify and report suspicious individuals to security.

techniques.name: Fake Pages
techniques.description:
The fraudster creates a web page that may mimic a legitimate website to fool victims into divulging information. This website may visually appear to be legitimate or have a URL that is like the legitimate website.
One example of this is to register a domain that looks or sounds like a legitimate website. If www.legitimatewebsite.com was the target the fraudster may register a website similar to www.legitimatewebsite.io or www.legitwebsite.com. Using this along with similar visual elements, the fraudster can fool victims into divulging information such as account name and password.

mitigations.name: Website Takedown Requests
mitigations.guidance: When a fake page is identified file a takedown request with the Website Host and DNS Registrar.

mitigations.name: DNS Registration
mitigations.guidance: Identify potential URLs that may be mistaken for the legitimate website and register them so they cannot be used by fraudsters.

detections.name: Network Traffic Attributes
detections.guidance: Monitor domain registration, certificate transparency logs, and phishing sites to identify sites established with your branding but designed to fool your customers into divulging information.

techniques.name: Acquire Database
techniques.description:
Fraudster will, through legitimate or illegal means, acquire databases that may be used for future operations. These databases may range from legitimate marketing information sold by reputable companies to data stolen from victims.
Some examples of databases that can be acquired to support operations are account databases, marketing information, gift card numbers, and personally identifiable information (PII).

mitigations.name: Password Policy
mitigations.guidance: Encourage using strong passwords with sufficient length and complexity. Discourage reusing passwords.

detections.name: Online Identities
detections.guidance: Subscribe to breach databases and monitor logins for usage of known or publicly compromised credentials.

references: Top 10 Digital Commerce Account Risks & How to Mitigate Them by Gunnar Peterson
Authentication and Access to Financial Institution Services and Systems

techniques.name: Gift Card Number Generation
techniques.description: Fraudster uses an algorithm or brute force to generate gift card numbers that can potentially be legitimate. This can be conducted by predicting or acquiring the algorithm used to generate gift card numbers and creating them. This can be used with Check Gift Card Balance to identify legitimate gift cards with funds for future use.

mitigations.name: Brute Force Resistant Gift Card Numbers
mitigations.guidance: Generate long and complicated gift card numbers that are resistant to prediction.

detections.guidance: This technique cannot be easily detected by organizational controls due to it occurring outside of the organization’s scope.

techniques.name: Password Reset
techniques.description:
Actors abuse the password reset functionality to verify whether an account exists on a website. If the website provides feedback that indicates the account does exist, the actor then proceeds to attempt a login for that account using exposed credentials. If the account does not exist, the actor does not submit a login request to avoid expending unnecessary resources on an invalid account.
Actors compromise the victim’s email account and then submit a password reset request to the targeted site. The actor is able to change the victim’s password to one of their choosing, allowing them access to the victim’s account.

mitigations.name: Neutral Feedback
mitigations.guidance: Do not provide feedback that notifies an actor if the account exists or does not exist on the website.

mitigations.name: Customer Notification
mitigations.guidance: Notify all available contacts on the account when a password is reset.

detections.name: Behavioral Attributes
detections.guidance: Monitor password reset endpoints for abnormal behavior.

detections.name: Velocity Attributes
detections.guidance: Identify automated attempts to validate a credential list by volume of attempts.

techniques.name: Proxy Abuse
techniques.description: Actors abuse legitimate or illegal proxy services that act as an intermediary for requests from clients seeking resources from other servers, effectively masking the fraudster’s IP address or other network attributes. Some examples of this are use of commercial VPN services, proxies through hosting providers, residential proxies, compromised machines such as botnets and malware infected hosts, and TOR services.

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention
mitigations.guidance: Block traffic from known proxies, TOR 7exit nodes and infected machines.

detections.name: Network Traffic Attributes
detections.guidance: Aggregate IP addresses to identify the common carriers / autonomous system numbers. Establish normal and abnormal behavior for traffic originating from those networks.

techniques.name: Third Party Supplier Manipulation
techniques.description: A supplier or manufacturer knowingly produces and distributes nongenuine goods with the intent (or willful disregard of the likelihood) that these items will be returned to legitimate retailers for refunds, store credit, or replacements, thereby monetizing counterfeits via the retailer’s returns channel and shifting losses to the merchant. This scheme often leverages high demand SKUs and categories with permissive return policies to maximize refund yield and minimize detection.

mitigations.name: Law Enforcement
mitigations.guidance: Report known counterfeiters or other confirmed illegal activity to Law Enforcement for action.

detections.name: Controlled Purchase
detections.guidance: Purchase items from Third Party Supplier to identify indicators of fraud.

detections.name: Transaction Data
detections.guidance: Identify indicators of counterfeit or fake items such as poor packaging or labeling with incorrect or repeating serial numbers.

detections.name: Time-Based Attributes
detections.guidance: Identify returns that happen quickly. This can range from a few minutes from purchase to a day depending on fraudster behavior.

detections.name: Velocity Attributes
detections.guidance: Fraudsters will attempt a high number of returns at once. This may be multiples of same item or different items.

techniques.name: Fake Receipt Generation
techniques.description: A fraudulent receipt created by a fraudster that appears legitimate. The primary purpose is to fabricate proof of purchase or transaction to deceive systems, individuals, or institutions and often to claim refunds, reimbursements, or validate false returns.

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention
mitigations.guidance: Validate the receipt with store records (preferably by electronic scan). Do not permit use of receipts without validation of store-controlled records.

mitigations.name: Training and Awareness
mitigations.guidance: Identify fake receipts, which may appear visually different.

detections.name: Transaction Data
detections.guidance: Identify refunds that do not have proper proof of purchase.

detections.name: Velocity Attributes
detections.guidance: A large volume of receipts may obscure or overlap with a genuine receipt. A large number of items on the receipt.

techniques.name: Insider Recruitment
techniques.description: A form of social engineering, this technique involves fraudsters enlisting employees, typically in customer service, logistics, or returns processing, to help execute fraudulent return schemes from within the organization. These insiders are incentivized with payments or a share of the refund value to manipulate internal systems, such as marking items as undelivered, falsifying damage claims, or overriding verification protocols. Recruitment often begins on social platforms like Telegram, LinkedIn, or even customer service contact channels with communication quickly shifting to encrypted channels to avoid detection. Once embedded, insiders can process large volumes of fraudulent refunds, making the scheme highly scalable and difficult to trace.

mitigations.name: Training and Awareness
mitigations.guidance: Train employees to recognize recruitment attempts and remind them of their role, ethical agreements, and consequences.

mitigations.name: Escalation
mitigations.guidance: Require secondary approvals for sensitive actions that can be taken on behalf of customers to limit damage an insider could perform.

detections.name: Behavioral Attributes
detections.guidance: Monitor employees’ interactions with other employees and discussions regarding potential payment or other ways to receive value for fraudulent activity. Insiders may attempt to hire employees to support their activity. Identify employees’ excessive referrals and the quality of those referrals. For call center or chat-based customer service operations, recruiters will often engage with many customer service representatives to find one who is willing or vulnerable. Identify customer attempts to offer money, jobs, or other reimbursement for actions taken at the retail store.

detections.name: Video Surveillance Systems
detections.guidance: Use video surveillance system to identify and record suspicious activity for correlation as fraudsters may commit actions over a long period.

techniques.name: Impersonation Of Retail Employee
techniques.description: A form of social engineering, this technique in returns fraud involves fraudsters posing as store staff, either physically, over the phone, or online, to manipulate return processes and bypass verification protocols. They may dress like employees, use fake IDs, or spoof contact details to gain trust and access, often requesting unauthorized refunds or overrides. In more advanced schemes, real employees are recruited to impersonate others or approve fraudulent returns, making fraud harder to detect and more scalable.

mitigations.name: Identity Verification
mitigations.guidance: Establish identification and authentication procedures to prove someone is an employee in person or remotely.

mitigations.name: Training and Awareness
mitigations.guidance: Train employees in stores to recognize impersonation attempts, posing as an employee, someone from headquarters, or a legitimate third party such as contractors.

mitigations.name: Escalation
mitigations.guidance: Require secondary approvals for sensitive actions that the fraudster may ask employees to perform.

detections.name: Behavioral Attributes
detections.guidance: Monitor employees’ interactions with other employees and discussions regarding potential payment or other ways to receive value for fraudulent activity. Insiders may attempt to hire employees to support their activity. Identify employees’ excessive referrals and the quality of those referrals. For call center or chat-based customer service operations, recruiters will often engage with many customer service representatives to find one who is willing or vulnerable. Identify customer attempts to offer money, jobs, or other reimbursements for actions taken at the retail store.

detections.name: Video Surveillance Systems
detections.guidance: Use video surveillance systems to identify and record suspicious activity for correlation, as fraudsters may commit actions over a long period. Correlate suspicious individuals across multiple stores to identify fraudsters.

techniques.name: Shoplifting
techniques.description:
Taking items from a store without paying for them. Shoplifting can range from concealing items in personal clothing or bags to swapping price tags to make items appear cheaper. Items shoplifted to support fraud are typically high value, small in size and easy to resell.
Examples of commonly stolen items to support fraud are Gift Cards, Electronics, and Luxury Goods.

mitigations.name: Satchel Control
mitigations.guidance: Control the size and type of satchels that are permitted inside the store.

mitigations.name: Anti-theft Prevention
mitigations.guidance: Additional physical protection of products from theft such as locked shelving, containers, and vending machines, and storing items behind checkout counter.

mitigations.name: Security Guards
mitigations.guidance: At physical locations, use security guards to identify and deter shoplifting.

detections.name: Anti-theft security tags
detections.guidance: Attach a device to items that will cause an alarm if removed from the store without authorization.

detections.name: Video Surveillance Systems
detections.guidance: Monitor video feeds for suspicious activity around high value items.

references: Detecting and Reporting the Illicit Financial Flows Tied to Organized Theft Groups (OTG) and Organized Retail Crime (ORC)

techniques.name: Gift Card Extortion
techniques.description:
The fraudster obtains gift cards through coercion of a victim. This can involve many forms, including threats of violence, property damage, harm to reputation, or unwarranted government action, unlike robbery or theft where property is taken without consent.
A fraudster may pretend to be a representative of the government to coerce a victim through a fear response. They may convince a victim that they must purchase gift cards with their own funds and turn the gift card over to the fraudster.
Another common extortion scam is a fraudster pretending to be a relative of a victim who is being held against their will whether by criminals or a foreign government. They then convince the victim to purchase gift cards as restitution or a bribe to release their family member.

mitigations.name: Primary Gift Card Lock In
mitigations.guidance: When a gift card is purchased, lock the gift card into the identity of the purchaser. Do not allow another person to use the gift card without identity verification or authentication.

mitigations.name: Login Required
mitigations.guidance: Require an account before permitting purchase of or transfer of a gift card.

mitigations.name: Gift Card Purchase Limit
mitigations.guidance: Enforce limits of quantity and/or the value that may be purchased by an interaction or person.

mitigations.name: Training and Awareness
mitigations.guidance: Consumer fraud awareness and education campaigns, signage, pop-ups, and other forms of communication.

detections.name: Velocity Attributes
detections.guidance: Monitor the purchase of gift cards by value and quantity from an individual by a predetermined value and/or time frame.

detections.name: Behavioral Attributes
detections.guidance: Monitor for out-of-character purchases of an individual and their lifestyle.

references: Detecting and Reporting the Illicit Financial Flows Tied to Organized Theft Groups (OTG) and Organized Retail Crime (ORC)
Avoiding and Reporting Gift Card Scams

techniques.name: Check Gift Card Balance
techniques.description: The fraudster may abuse legitimate functions to confirm a gift card is active and has funds. To reduce overhead, retailers may have autonomous systems for gift card owners and recipients to check if their gift card is usable and has value. These systems are generally available to the public for interaction.
sub_techniques: Application FT1103.001, Phone Verification FT1103.002, In Store Gift Card Verification FT1103.003

mitigations.name: Login Required
mitigations.guidance: Require authentication before displaying gift card status or value.

mitigations.name: Access Code Required
mitigations.guidance: Require an access code that is separate from the gift card number before revealing the status and funds on the gift cards.

mitigations.name: Online Location Data
mitigations.guidance: Some physical locations should not be able to check gift card balance. Some locations may also be the source of repeated fraud attempts. Prevent the ability to check gift card status and funds based on locations.

mitigations.name: Phone Number
mitigations.guidance: Automatically block phone numbers related to VOIP services and phone numbers that have been known to be used to perpetrate fraud.

detections.name: Network Traffic Attributes
detections.guidance: Monitor for Network Traffic Attributes such as IP Address, DNS Name, ASN, and other digital location attributes especially if some of these sources have known fraud activity or have a high risk of fraud activity.

detections.name: Time-Based Attributes
detections.guidance: Based on the location of your operations, monitor for activities that occur during off hours.

detections.name: Device Attributes
detections.guidance: Monitor device factors such as device type, user agent string, operating system, cookies.

detections.name: Velocity Attributes
detections.guidance: Monitor for number of requests based on a predetermined number of requests over a set amount of time.

detections.name: VOIP Attribute
detections.guidance: Monitor for use of VOIP numbers that are not tied to a physical landline or mobile phone.

techniques.name: Check Gift Card Balance: Application
techniques.description:
The fraudster may iteratively probe Web Applications using built-in functions in the Applications to confirm the gift card is active and has funds. The fraudster may use gift card numbers that are generated by brute force guessing, purchased from a source, or gathered from victims.
A fraudster may purchase a large amount of gift card numbers on the dark web. They will use the Web Application built-in Function and in a manual or automated fashion check to see if the gift card is active and has funds. This information can be used in future operations to convert the gift card into usable funds for the fraudster.

mitigations.name: Login Required
mitigations.guidance: Require authentication before displaying gift card status or value.

mitigations.name: Access Code Required
mitigations.guidance: Require an access code that is separate from the gift card number before revealing the status and funds on the gift cards.

detections.guidance: Monitor device factors such as device type, user agent string, operating system, cookies.

detections.name: Velocity Attributes
detections.guidance: Monitor for number of requests based on a predetermined number of requests over a set amount of time.

techniques.name: Check Gift Card Balance: Phone Verification
techniques.description: The fraudster may use a retailer-provided phone service to confirm a gift card is active and has funds. The fraudster may use gift card numbers that are generated by brute force guessing, purchased from a source, or gathered from victims.

mitigations.name: Access Code Required
mitigations.guidance: Require an access code that is separate from the gift card number before revealing the status and funds on the gift cards.

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention
mitigations.guidance: Automatically block phone numbers related to VOIP services and phone numbers that have been known to be used to perpetrate fraud.

detections.name: Time-Based Attributes
detections.guidance: Based on the location of your operations, monitor for activities that occur during off hours.

detections.name: VOIP Attribute
detections.guidance: Monitor for use of VOIP numbers that are not tied to a physical landline or mobile phone.

techniques.name: Verification
techniques.description: The fraudster uses legitimate functions inside a bricks-and-mortar store to verify status of gift cards. The fraudster may use Kiosks, Checkout, or Customer service to verify legitimacy of a gift card.

mitigations.name: Access Code Required
mitigations.guidance: Require an access code that is separate from the gift card number before revealing the status and funds on the gift cards.

detections.name: Velocity Attributes
detections.guidance: Monitor for gift cards a person is attempting to verify.

techniques.name: Valid Accounts
techniques.description:
The fraudster may obtain, create and abuse accounts to gain access, elevate access, or control a resource. Since these credentials are generally legitimate, they may be used to bypass access controls in place to protect resources. This can also be used to achieve persistence in a system.
One example of this is if a fraudster gains control over a loyalty account. The fraudster can control the spending of loyalty points to buy items to support monetization. If gift cards are tied to the accounts, this may also be a method to control gift card use.
sub_techniques: Fraudulent Account FT1104.001, Fraudulent Account Update FT1104.002, Authorized Account Abuse FT1104.003

mitigations.name: Multi-Factor Authentication
mitigations.guidance: Use multiple forms of authentication such as username and password paired with a One-time Passcode before permitting access. Use passkeys linked to a known physical device as authentication factor. Require identity verification upon detection of access requests that are significantly different than what is expected for the individual.

mitigations.name: Password Policy
mitigations.guidance: Encourage using strong passwords with sufficient length and complexity. Discourage reusing passwords.

detections.name: Network Traffic Attributes
detections.guidance: Monitor for Network Traffic Attributes such as IP Address, DNS Name, ASN, and other digital location attributes especially if some of these sources have known fraud activity or have a high risk of fraud activity.

detections.name: Time-Based Attributes
detections.guidance: Based on the location of your operations, monitor for activities that occur during off hours.

detections.name: Device Attributes
detections.guidance: Monitor device factors such as device type, user agent string, operating system, cookies.

detections.name: Behavioral Attributes
detections.guidance: Monitor for access attempts and purchases that are significantly different from known good behavior for each customer.

references: Top 10 Digital Commerce Account Risks & How to Mitigate Them by Gunnar Peterson
Authentication and Access to Financial Institution Services and Systems

techniques.name: Valid Accounts: Fraudulent Account
techniques.description:
The fraudster uses a legitimate resource to create an account for malicious usage. These accounts may be used for reconnaissance and to probe the defenses of the victim’s applications.
One example of this is if a fraudster creates an account with fake information. Using this as a foothold the fraudster may gather information on the application itself such as naming convention, loyalty points, and other information that may be used to monetize the account.

mitigations.name: Multi-Factor Authentication
mitigations.guidance: Before permitting account changes, use multiple forms of authentication such as username and password paired with a One-time Passcode before permitting access. If relevant, send confirmatory message to the original contact fields (e.g., original email address, phone number, street address).

detections.name: Network Traffic Attributes

detections.guidance: Based on the location of your operations, monitor for activities that occur during off hours.

detections.guidance: Monitor device factors such as device type, user agent string, operating system, cookies.

detections.name: Velocity Attributes
detections.guidance: Monitor for accounts that are created quickly in succession from the same location or with similar features.

references: Top 10 Digital Commerce Account Risks & How to Mitigate Them by Gunnar Peterson

techniques.name: Valid Accounts: Fraudulent Account Update
techniques.description:
The fraudster makes a change to an account without the knowledge of the account holder.
One example of this is if a fraudster convinces a helpdesk to update the phone number of a legitimate account to one they control. The fraudster can then use this to reset the password or otherwise authenticate to control the victim’s account.

mitigations.name: Multi-Factor Authentication
mitigations.guidance: Use multiple forms of authentication such as username and password paired with a One-time Passcode before permitting access. Require identity verification upon detection of access requests that are significantly different than what is expected for the individual. Send confirmatory message to the original contact fields (e.g., original email address, phone number, street address).

detections.guidance: Monitor for Network Traffic Attributes such as IP Address, DNS Name, ASN, and other digital location attributes especially if some of these sources have known fraud activity or have a high risk of fraud activity.

detections.guidance: Based on the location of your operations, monitor for activities that occur during off hours.

detections.guidance: Monitor device factors such as device type, user agent string, operating system, cookies.

detections.name: Velocity Attributes
detections.guidance: Monitor for accounts that are created quickly in succession from the same location or with similar features.

detections.name: Online Identities
detections.guidance: Monitor for account creations with suspicious names that do not appear legitimate. Some examples are ABCD, AAA, QAZ, etc.

references: Top 10 Digital Commerce Account Risks & How to Mitigate Them by Gunnar Peterson

techniques.name: Valid Accounts: Authorized Account Abuse
techniques.description: The fraudster persuades a legitimate customer to grant access to their account, enabling the fraudster to leverage a seasoned profile with an established purchase history and associated metadata. This tactic helps bypass or weaken fraud detection controls.

mitigations.guidance: Before permitting account changes, use multiple forms of authentication such as username and password paired with a One-time Passcode before permitting access. If relevant, send confirmatory message to the original contact fields (e.g., original email address, phone number, street address).

techniques.name: Credential Stuffing
techniques.description:
Fraudsters abuse a variety of web automation tools to automate login attempts using credential lists known as “combolists.” Web automation serves a legitimate purpose in web application development and testing, but commercial projects can be abused by threat actors for illicit activity.
Fraudsters develop custom credential stuffing tools to automate login attempts. These tools can be site-specific or configurable via files known as “configs” which are then either sold or shared in underground communities. These tools range from simple scripts where technical details for the transaction are coded into the script itself, to fully configurable tools where actors can insert their own variables and other parameters into the automation.

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention
mitigations.guidance: Many commercial services provide bot detection and mitigation, often incorporated into content delivery networks and other management packages. Commonly available tooling includes default technical indicators which should be mitigated at the edge and automatically denied.

detections.name: Velocity Attributes
detections.guidance: Monitor for surges in login attempts and other anomalous activity. Monitor the response to login attempts where a surge in attempts to access accounts that do not exist at the target organization is a strong indicator of automated credential stuffing.

detections.name: Behavioral Attributes
detections.guidance: Monitor for repeated patterns of activity post-login that is an indicator that the activity is automated.

references: Top 10 Digital Commerce Account Risks & How to Mitigate Them by Gunnar Peterson

techniques.name: Gift Card Return
techniques.description:
The fraudster converts an illicitly acquired or invalid gift card for a legitimate gift card.
For example, a fraudster illicitly obtains a gift card. Through social engineering or taking advantage of a retailer’s legitimate system, they transfer the value from the illicitly obtained gift card to a new gift card that the fraudster legitimately owns.

mitigations.name: Return Limit
mitigations.guidance: Do not exchange gift cards over a pre-determined value.

detections.name: Transaction Data
detections.guidance: Identify suspicious purchases and returns by gift card numbers.

references: Detecting and Reporting the Illicit Financial Flows Tied to Organized Theft Groups (OTG) and Organized Retail Crime (ORC)

techniques.name: Gift Card Merge
techniques.description:
The fraudster obtains a gift card through legitimate means. Using a retailer-provided method they transfer value from an illicitly obtained gift to the legitimate gift cards.
For example, a fraudster purchases a legitimate gift card with a value of $5. They illicitly obtain multiple gift cards with values of $100 and $150. Using a legitimate retailer feature they combine gift cards. The values of the illicitly obtained gift cards are added to the legitimate one. The fraudster added $250 to their $5 gift card. They now have $255 on their legitimate gift card.

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention
mitigations.guidance: Do not permit merging of gift cards.

mitigations.name: Login Required
mitigations.guidance: Require authentication before permitting transfer of gift card value.

mitigations.name: Access Code Required
mitigations.guidance: Require an access code before permitting transfer of gift card value.

detections.name: Transaction Data
detections.guidance: Identify suspicious transfer of value from gift cards to other gift cards.

detections.name: Velocity Attributes
detections.guidance: Identify suspicious transfers from many gift cards to one gift card. For example if 20 gift cards with value of $5 are added to a single gift card.

techniques.name: Gift Card Tampering
techniques.description:
Fraudster takes physical possession of an unactivated gift card and takes the information that allows them to control the gift card when it is funded and activated.
An example is a fraudster steals gift cards from a store. They copy down the pertinent information needed to control the gift card and verify funds such as gift card number and security pin. The fraudster then repackages the gift card and returns it to the store. When a victim purchases the gift card and loads value, the fraudster can spend the funds on the gift card without the victim’s awareness.

mitigations.name: Primary Gift Card Lock in
mitigations.guidance: For gift cards, lock the Gift Card into the identity of the purchaser. Do not allow another person to use the gift card without identity verification or authentication.

mitigations.name: Login Required
mitigations.guidance: For gift cards, require an account before permitting purchase of or transfer.

mitigations.name: Anti-theft Prevention
mitigations.guidance: Store gift cards behind checkout counter to limit theft.

mitigations.name: Security Guard
mitigations.guidance: At physical locations, use security guards to identify instances of fraudsters stealing gift cards and/or returning tampered gift cards.

detections.name: Video Surveillance Systems
detections.guidance: At physical locations, use video surveillance to identify instances of fraudsters stealing gift cards and/or returning tampered gift cards

references: Detecting and Reporting the Illicit Financial Flows Tied to Organized Theft Groups (OTG) and Organized Retail Crime (ORC)

techniques.name: Gift Card Redemption
techniques.description:
The fraudster obtains a gift card through legitimate or illicit means and purchases an item.
One example of this is a fraudster uses a gift card to purchase a high-value easy-to-sell item such as jewelry or electronics. The fraudster then can monetize these items through various strategies such as resale or drop shipping.

mitigations.name: Primary Gift Card Lock in
mitigations.guidance: For gift cards, lock the gift card into the identity of the purchaser. Do not allow another person to use the gift card without identity verification or authentication.

mitigations.name: Login Required
mitigations.guidance: For gift cards, require an account before permitting purchase of or transfer.

detections.name: Transaction Data
detections.guidance: Identify suspicious purchases of commonly resold items with potentially illicitly obtained gift cards.

references: Detecting and Reporting the Illicit Financial Flows Tied to Organized Theft Groups (OTG) and Organized Retail Crime (ORC)

techniques.name: Loyalty Points Abuse
techniques.description:
The fraudster converts loyalty points into items or gift cards that can be used for monetization.
One example of this is a fraudster successfully compromises a victim’s account through means such as Social Engineering. They can convert the victim’s loyalty points into a gift card that the fraudster controls. This gift card can be further used for monetization.

mitigations.name: Multi-Factor Authentication
mitigations.guidance: Use multiple forms of authentication such as username and password paired with a One-time Passcode before permitting access. Require identity verification upon detection of access requests that are significantly different than what is expected for the individual.

mitigations.name: Password Policy
mitigations.guidance: Encourage using strong passwords with sufficient length and complexity. Discourage reusing passwords.

detections.name: Network Traffic Attributes
detections.guidance: Monitor for Network Traffic Attributes such as IP Address, DNS Name, ASN, and other digital location attributes especially if some of these sources have known fraud activity or have a high risk of fraud activity.

detections.name: Time-Based Attributes
detections.guidance: Based on the location of your operations, monitor for activities that occur during off hours.

detections.name: Device Attributes
detections.guidance: Monitor device factors such as device type, user agent string, operating system, cookies.

detections.name: Behavioral Attributes
detections.guidance: Monitor for access attempts and purchases that are significantly different from known good behavior for each customer.

techniques.name: Item Manipulation
techniques.description: Fraudster returns merchandise to a retailer under deceptive circumstances to obtain monetary refunds, store credit, replacement goods, or has somehow extracted value from the merchandise. This technique involves presenting an item at the point of return (altered, incomplete, counterfeit, or previously used) while misrepresenting its condition or origin.

mitigations.name: Item Condition & Tag Checks
mitigations.guidance: Ensure item is returned with all its components such as packaging, accessories, and documentation in good condition. Verify additional attributes such as weight, general wear and tear. Scuffs on screws Reapplied tape Do not accept returns that are missing components or may be suspicious.

mitigations.name: Anti-theft Prevention
mitigations.guidance: Use unique serial numbers or RFID tags tied to the original transaction record. Verify serial numbers / digital product IDs upon return. Apply tamper-proof seals or packaging that are difficult to replicate.

mitigations.name: Return Limit
mitigations.guidance: Require original packaging in return policy for high-value items. Shorten return windows for high-risk categories (electronics, luxury goods). Deny returns to guests or tenders with a history of abuse or suspected abuse.

mitigations.name: Proof of Purchase
mitigations.guidance: Require receipts and ID for high-value returns.

mitigations.name: Restocking Fees
mitigations.guidance: Charge fees for high-risk categories.

mitigations.name: Training and Awareness
mitigations.guidance: Train associates to identify mismatched logos, misspelled labels, or damaged packaging.

mitigations.name: Escalation
mitigations.guidance: Implement escalation paths for suspicious returns.

detections.name: Transaction Data
detections.guidance: Match returned product identifiers (IMEI, serial, RFID) to the original purchase record.

detections.name: Behavioral Attributes
detections.guidance: Profiles or tenders with high rates of returns in specific categories.

detections.name: Device Attributes
detections.guidance: Use graph or link analysis to find connected devices, IPs, or payment tenders and label them as suspicious for future tracking.

detections.name: Online Identities
detections.guidance: Use graph or link analysis to find connected accounts.

techniques.name: Item Manipulation: Harvesting
techniques.description:
Fraudster harvests valuable components of an item and returns the merchandise for a full refund.
For example, a fraudster purchases a computer. They harvest valuable components such as the graphics processor and CPU. They then return the item to the store and receive full value of the purchase but have stolen the components.
Another example: A fraudster purchases a console system that comes with redeemable points or other single use credit that is meant for the purchaser. They steal and redeem this credit then return the console for full value.

mitigations.name: Item Condition & Tag Checks
mitigations.guidance: Ensure item is returned with all its components such as packaging, accessories, and documentation in good condition. Verify additional attributes such as weight, general wear and tear. Scuffs on screws Reapplied tape Do not accept returns that are missing components or may be suspicious.

mitigations.name: Anti-theft Prevention
mitigations.guidance: Apply tamper-proof seals or packaging that are difficult to replicate.

mitigations.name: Restocking Fees
mitigations.guidance: Charge fees for high-risk categories.

detections.name: Behavioral Attributes
detections.guidance: Profiles or tenders with high rates of returns in specific categories.

techniques.name: Item Manipulation: Switch Merchandise
techniques.description:
A fraudster returns a different item, a broken item, or a counterfeit item for resources such as gift cards, store credit, or cash.
For example, a fraudster may purchase an item they already own that is broken. They then keep the new merchandise and put the broken item into the box of the new purchase. They return the broken item for full monetary value.
Another example is that a fraudster may purchase an item online, begin an online return and ship a different item, or other material that is similar in weight or size. The fraudster then keeps the purchased item and receives monetary value of the returned item.

mitigations.name: Anti-theft Prevention
mitigations.guidance: Use unique serial numbers or RFID tags tied to the original transaction record. Verify serial numbers / digital product IDs upon return. Apply tamper-proof seals or packaging that are difficult to replicate.

mitigations.name: Return Limit
mitigations.guidance: Require original packaging in return policy for high-value items. Shorten return windows for high-risk categories (electronics, luxury goods). Deny returns to guests or tenders with a history of abuse or suspected abuse.

mitigations.name: Proof of Purchase
mitigations.guidance: Require receipts and ID for high-value returns.

mitigations.name: Restocking Fees
mitigations.guidance: Charge fees for returning high-risk categories.

mitigations.name: Training and Awareness
mitigations.guidance: Train associates to identify mismatched logos, misspelled labels or damaged packaging.

mitigations.name: Escalation
mitigations.guidance: Implement Escalation paths for suspicious returns.

detections.name: Transaction Data
detections.guidance: Match returned product identifiers (IMEI, serial, RFID) to the original purchase record.

detections.name: Behavioral Attributes
detections.guidance: Identify accounts or tenders with repeated returns in high-counterfeit categories.

detections.name: Device Attributes
detections.guidance: Use graph or link analysis to find connected devices, IP addresses, or payment tenders and label them as suspicious for future tracking.

detections.name: Online Identities
detections.guidance: Use graph or link analysis to find connected accounts.

techniques.name: Returns Process Exploitation
techniques.description:
A fraudster abuses a retailer’s returns system to receive the value of an item. They may claim an item is damaged or never arrived.
For example, a fraudster purchases an item and has it delivered to their house. Though the merchandise arrived, they fraudulently claim the item has never arrived or was damaged in transit. They abuse the retailer’s claims system to receive a refund as well as keeping the delivered item.
sub_techniques: Shipping Manipulation FT1207.001, Damaged Shipment FT1207.002

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention
mitigations.guidance: Flag customers that make too many returns and delay or deny returns.

mitigations.name: Restocking Fees
mitigations.guidance: Impose a fee for returns.

mitigations.name: Delayed Reimbursement
mitigations.guidance: Delay reimbursement for a specific amount of time or until the return is verified.

mitigations.name: Proof of Purchase
mitigations.guidance: Require proof of purchase such as a receipt before permitting return.

detections.name: Transaction Data
detections.guidance: Record serial numbers to make sure refunds match the product.

detections.name: Behavioral Attributes
detections.guidance: Identify fraudsters that make repeat or frequent returns. Identify fraudsters attempting to refund online and in stores.

detections.name: Device Attributes
detections.guidance: Identify devices such as a single phone or computer used for many return attempts.

techniques.name: Returns Process Exploitation: Shipping Manipulation
techniques.description: Fraudster purchases an item with the intent to return the item. They request a return from the retailer and tamper with the return label, resulting in a lost package. The fraudster does not return the original item, but an item with similar weight and size. The retailer in good faith refunds the fraudster as soon as the return is initiated. The fraudster now possesses the merchandise as well as the value of the refund.

mitigations.name: Delivery Confirmation
mitigations.guidance: Only refund after the item is received and verified.

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention
mitigations.guidance: Flag customers that make too many returns and delay or deny returns.

mitigations.name: Return Limit
mitigations.guidance: Restrict fast refunds on high-risk items like electronics.

mitigations.name: Delayed Reimbursement
mitigations.guidance: Delay reimbursement for a specific amount of time or until the return is verified.

detections.name: Behavioral Attributes
detections.guidance: Identify fraudsters that make repeat or frequent delivery-based returns.

detections.name: Transaction Data
detections.guidance: Match refund claims with shipping records.

detections.name: Device Attributes
detections.guidance: Identify devices such as a single phone or computer used for many return attempts.

techniques.name: Returns Process Exploitation: Damaged Shipment
techniques.description:
A fraudster orders multiple items in one shipment and then falsely claims that damage to one item rendered the entire order unusable (e.g., leakage, shattered glass, food contamination). They request an order-level refund or reshipment rather than a partial remedy, exploiting lenient damage policies and limited evidence requirements.
One example is when a fraudster orders printer ink, toner and a laptop, then claims the toner exploded during shipping and damaged the laptop. The fraudster requests a refund for all items while keeping them.

mitigations.name: Proof of Damage
mitigations.guidance: Require customers to submit photos or video evidence of damage. Require the physical return of damaged goods before issuing a refund.

mitigations.name: Enhanced Packaging
mitigations.guidance: Isolate items that could leak or cause contamination into separate packages. Use waterproof packaging or tamper-proof seals.

mitigations.name: Return Limit
mitigations.guidance: Limit the amount that can be refunded without requiring the item to be physically returned.

detections.name: Behavioral Attributes
detections.guidance: Flag customers with repeated claims tied to specific accounts, addresses, and/or payment identities. Monitor for claims made on first-time orders by new customers.

detections.name: Velocity Attributes
detections.guidance: Monitor for frequent damage claims of specific items.

techniques.name: Wardrobing
techniques.description:
A fraudster buys merchandise (often apparel, footwear, or accessories) intending to temporarily use or wear the item for an event, photo shoot, or short-term need. After use, the fraudster returns the item, exploiting return policies. The retailer incurs losses through inventory depreciation, sanitation costs, and resale markdowns, as returned items often cannot be sold as new.
For example, a fraudster has an upcoming special event such as a wedding. They purchase expensive dresses, jewelry, and other accessories with no intent of keeping them. After they wear the merchandise to their event, they return the items to the store for a refund.

mitigations.name: Return Limit
mitigations.guidance: Deny returns on worn, washed, or tag-removed items. Shorten return windows for seasonal / fashion merchandise.

mitigations.name: Restocking Fees
mitigations.guidance: Apply Restocking Fees to high-value apparel items.

detections.name: Velocity Attributes
detections.guidance: Profiles or tenders with high rates of returns in specific categories.

detections.name: Item Condition & Tag Checks
detections.guidance: Inspect the item being returned for missing original packaging, tags, or signs of use (stains, scuffs).

detections.name: Anti-theft Prevention
detections.guidance: Use tamper-proof tagging that would leave a detectable residue that the item has been worn. RFID tagging to validate item being returned was purchased within the return window (prevents purchasing a new item and returning old).

techniques.name: Resale
techniques.description:
The fraudster exchanges the illicitly obtained items or gift cards with another person or organization in exchange for liquid funds.
For example, a fraudster may steal jewelry worth $100. Using a third party market such as Facebook Marketplace, they sell the illicitly obtained jewelry for $80, converting the item to currency the fraudster controls.
sub_techniques: Drop Shipping FT1301.001, Unwitting Buyer FT1301.002

techniques.name: Resale: Drop Shipping
techniques.description:
The fraudster will use a third party to ship directly to a customer.
For example, to obfuscate the legitimacy of the gift card, the fraudster will store gift cards with a third-party partner who will list and manage their gift cards. A buyer will purchase the gift card from the third party. The buyer will receive illegally obtained gift cards.

mitigations.name: Primary Gift Card Lock in
mitigations.guidance: For gift cards, lock the gift card into the identity of the purchaser. Do not allow another person to use the gift card without identity verification or authentication.

mitigations.name: Login Required
mitigations.guidance: For gift cards, require an account before permitting purchase of or transfer.

detections.name: Transaction data
detections.guidance: Monitor for anomalous purchases of easily monetized items such as Electronics and Luxury Goods.

references: Detecting and Reporting the Illicit Financial Flows Tied to Organized Theft Groups (OTG) and Organized Retail Crime (ORC)

techniques.name: Resale: Unwitting Buyer
techniques.description: The fraudster sells the illicitly obtained goods or resources to an unwitting buyer.

mitigations.name: Primary Gift Card Lock in
mitigations.guidance: For gift cards, lock the gift card into the identity of the purchaser. Do not allow another person to use the gift card without identity verification or authentication.

mitigations.name: Login Required

detections.name: Market Resale Data
detections.guidance: Monitor for anomalous sales of serialized items and gift cards in third party locations and other repositories.

references: Detecting and Reporting the Illicit Financial Flows Tied to Organized Theft Groups (OTG) and Organized Retail Crime (ORC)

techniques.name: Marketplace Exploitation
techniques.description:
Fraudulent sellers pose as legitimate marketplace accounts and exploit drop shipping to shift financial loss and reputational damage onto retailers.
These sellers may deliver counterfeit, damaged, or no goods at all, causing customers to request refunds or initiate chargebacks, which the retailer absorbs.
Fraudsters often use stolen payment methods, fake or nonexistent addresses, and may intercept packages or “double dip” by keeping goods while claiming non-delivery. This tactic enables criminals to convert illicit funds into legitimate cash while leaving retailers with monetary losses, operational burdens, and customer dissatisfaction.
sub_techniques: Fraudulent Delivery FT1302.001, Fraudulent Seller FT1302.002

mitigations.name: Delivery Confirmation
mitigations.guidance: Only refund after the item is received and verified.

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention
mitigations.guidance: Validate address is legitimate and do not deliver to unlisted addresses.

mitigations.name: Blacklist Known High-Risk Addresses
mitigations.guidance: Maintain a blacklist of shipping and billing addresses tied to prior fraud, freight forwarders, or reshipping operations, and block or hold orders directed to them.

mitigations.name: Require Signature on Delivery
mitigations.guidance: Require signature confirmation at delivery for high-value or high-risk orders to establish proof of receipt and counter fraudulent non-delivery claims.

detections.name: Network Traffic Attributes
detections.guidance: Identify mismatch between Network Traffic Attributes such as IP geo location against the billing and shipping address.

detections.name: Location Attributes
detections.guidance: Identify mismatch between billing and shipping address.

detections.name: Behavioral Attributes
detections.guidance: Refund returns only to the method of purchase.

techniques.name: Marketplace Exploitation: Fraudulent Delivery
techniques.description:
The fraudster places an order using a fraudulent, fake, incorrect, or nonexistent shipping address. This could be, but is not limited to: a fake street number, a real street but non-existent apartment number, an abandoned property, or a vacant lot. The fraudster may use stolen credit cards or other illicit resources to pay for the item.
If the item is successfully delivered, the fraudster may steal the item from the real, but fraudulent location or a consolidated mailroom such as an apartment, business, or delivery service.
The fraudster may attempt to intercept the item from the delivery service to gain control of the item.
The fraudster may “double dip” and intercept the package to keep the goods and claim non-delivery.

mitigations.name: Delivery Confirmation
mitigations.guidance: Only refund after the item is received and verified.

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention
mitigations.guidance: Validate address is legitimate and do not deliver to unlisted addresses.

mitigations.guidance: Maintain a blacklist of shipping and billing addresses tied to prior fraud, freight forwarders, or reshipping operations, and block or hold orders directed to them.

techniques.name: Marketplace Exploitation: Fraudulent Seller
techniques.description:
A fraudulent seller is an account operating on (or connected to) your storefront/marketplace that appears legitimate but uses drop shipping to execute scams that shift loss, reputational damage, and chargebacks onto your retail brand.
A legitimate customer may buy an item from the reseller that is counterfeit, damaged, or inferior. This results in the customer returning the item for a full refund of the full cost of a legitimate item. In the event the item does not exist or it is not delivered, the customer will then initiate a refund. Both situations result in the retailer losing money, chargebacks, or returns.
A fraudster may work with the fraudulent seller to purchase the item with stolen funds or other illicit resources. The seller either does not deliver an item or delivers an inferior item, resulting in a return or chargeback. The seller is then able to convert stolen funds into legitimate cash.

mitigations.name: Delivery Confirmation
mitigations.guidance: Only refund after the item is received and verified.

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention
mitigations.guidance: Do not permit resellers to operate in your ecosystem without legitimate business credentials or sufficient time in market. Validate address is legitimate and do not deliver to unlisted addresses.

mitigations.name: Blacklist Known High-Risk Addresses
mitigations.guidance: Maintain a blacklist of shipping and billing addresses tied to prior fraud, freight forwarders, or reshipping operations, and block or hold orders directed to them.

mitigations.name: Require Signature on Delivery
mitigations.guidance: Require signature confirmation at delivery for high-value or high-risk orders to establish proof of receipt and counter fraudulent non-delivery claims.

mitigations.name: Behavioral Attributes
mitigations.guidance: Refund returns only to the method of purchase.

detections.name: Velocity Attributes
detections.guidance: Flag sellers with multiple returns or chargebacks.

techniques.name: Checkout

mitigations.guidance: Some physical locations should not be able to return items. Some locations may also be the source of repeated fraud attempts. Prevent the ability to return items for funds based on locations.

techniques.name: Fraudulent Refund
techniques.description: Deliberate exploitation of a retailer’s refund process to obtain financial gain or store credit without legitimate grounds. The fraudster initiates a return, often under false pretenses such as claiming damage, misrepresentation, or leveraging policy loopholes, and secures cash refunds, gift cards, or store credit.
sub_techniques: Refund to Gift Card FT1304.001, Double Refund FT1304.002, Non-Receipted Returns FT1304.003

mitigations.name: Return Limit
mitigations.guidance: Link each order to an individual refund. Restrict how many times a refund can be requested per order. Limit the number and total amount of non-receipted returns per customer. Limit the types of items that can be returned without a receipt. Only allow in-store credit or gift cards as a refund tender.

mitigations.name: Behavioral Attributes
mitigations.guidance: Stop refunds if the same order ID is already refunded.

mitigations.name: Escalation
mitigations.guidance: Escalate suspicious repeat attempts to returns.

mitigations.name: Identity Verification
mitigations.guidance: Require government-issued ID. Tie return transaction to customer profile for monitoring.

mitigations.name: Restocking Fees
mitigations.guidance: Impose fees on items being returned.

mitigations.name: Redemption Limits
mitigations.guidance: Limit the amount of store credit that can be used on a single transaction.

detections.name: Transaction Data
detections.guidance: Identify multiple refund requests for the same order. Check if item identifiers (IMEI, serial, RFID) can be associated with a prior purchase. Identify the same return in multiple stores and online.

detections.name: Behavioral Attributes
detections.guidance: Flag accounts that are doing frequent gift card refunds. Identify in person or Online Identities attempting gift card refund. Flag accounts attempting frequent non-receipted returns. Monitor for invalid government ID usage. Track items frequently returned without receipts at locations associated with high rates of theft. Compare items against inventory shortage reports.

detections.name: Device Attributes
detections.guidance: Detect repeat attempts from the same computer or phone submitting duplicate requests.

detections.name: Velocity Attributes
detections.guidance: Identify accounts requesting several refunds in a short time.

detections.name: Credit Redemption Behavior
detections.guidance: Monitor for the consolidation of in-store credit gift cards to purchase high-value items or issued to multiple identities (e.g. electronics).

techniques.name: Refund: Refund To Gift Card
techniques.description: Exploiting a retailer’s refund process by requesting that the refund value be issued as a gift card or store credit rather than returned to the original payment method. Fraudsters favor gift cards because they are highly liquid, easily transferable, and often lack the same fraud detection or traceability controls for credit or debit card refunds. Once obtained, these gift cards can be resold on secondary markets, exchanged for cash, or used to purchase high-value goods for sale, effectively converting fraudulent returns into fungible currency.

mitigations.name: Access Code Required
mitigations.guidance: Require an access code before permitting access to resources.

mitigations.name: Return Limit
mitigations.guidance: Limit the amount of money that can be refunded.

mitigations.name: Escalation
mitigations.guidance: Based on value require Escalation to manager.

detections.name: Transaction Data
detections.guidance: Record serial numbers for refunded gift cards.

detections.name: Behavioral Attributes
detections.guidance: Flag accounts doing frequent gift card refunds. Identify in person or Online Identities attempting gift card refund.

detections.name: Device Attributes
detections.guidance: Detect repeat attempts from the same computer or phone.

techniques.name: Refund: Double Refund
techniques.description: Fraudsters refund the same item multiple times either in multiple stores, online or some combination of both.

mitigations.name: Return Limit
mitigations.guidance: Link each order to an individual refund. Restrict how many times a refund can be requested per order.

mitigations.name: Escalation
mitigations.guidance: Escalate repeat attempts to return the same item to manager.

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention
mitigations.guidance: Stop refunds if the same order ID is already refunded.

detections.name: Transaction Data
detections.guidance: Identify multiple refund requests for the same order. Identify the same return in multiple stores and online.

detections.name: Behavioral Attributes
detections.guidance: Flag accounts doing frequent gift card refunds. Identify in person or Online Identities attempting gift card refund.

detections.name: Device Attributes
detections.guidance: Detect repeat attempts from the same computer or phone submitting duplicate requests.

detections.name: Velocity Attributes
detections.guidance: Identify accounts requesting several refunds in a short time.

techniques.name: Refund: Non-Receipted Returns
techniques.description: Fraudster intentionally misuses the returns process without a valid receipt (or other proof of purchase) to obtain cash refunds, store credit, gift cards, or replacements. The actor exploits no receipt allowances, low evidence thresholds, and minimal inspection.

mitigations.name: Return Limit
mitigations.guidance: Limit the number and total amount of non-receipted returns per customer. Limit the types of items that can be returned without a receipt. Only allow in-store credit or gift cards as a refund tender.

mitigations.name: Identity Verification
mitigations.guidance: Require government-issued ID. Tie return transaction to customer profile for monitoring.

mitigations.name: Restocking Fees
mitigations.guidance: Impose fees on items being returned that have no proof of purchase.

mitigations.name: Redemption Limits
mitigations.guidance: Limit the amount of store credit that can be used on a single transaction.

detections.name: Behavioral Attributes
detections.guidance: Flag accounts attempting frequent non-receipted returns. Monitor for invalid government ID usage. Track items frequently returned without receipts at locations associated with high rates of theft. Compare against inventory shortage reports.

detections.name: Transaction Data
detections.guidance: Check if item identifiers (IMEI, serial, RFID) can be associated with a prior purchase.

detections.name: Credit Redemption Behavior
detections.guidance: Monitor for the consolidation of in-store credit gift cards to purchase high value items or issued to multiple identities (e.g. electronics).

techniques.name: VOIP Abuse
techniques.description: Fraudsters leverage Voice over Internet Protocol (VOIP) services to mask or manipulate their true geographic location and identity during fraudulent transactions. By using VOIP numbers, they can appear to originate from a trusted region or local area, even when operating from a completely different country or jurisdiction. This tactic is designed to evade fraud detection systems that rely on phone number validation, geolocation checks, or call-back verification. These numbers may also be used on seemingly normal account creations.

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention
mitigations.guidance: Do not permit registration of VOIP numbers on accounts or other customer resources.

detections.name: VOIP Attribute
detections.guidance: Identify VOIP phone usage and correlate against customer profile. Identify high-risk VOIP numbers or multiple accounts with the same VOIP number in your database.

techniques.name: Digital Wallet Apps
techniques.description: Digital wallet applications (such as Apple Pay, Google Pay, and PayPal) are mobile or web-based platforms that store payment credentials and enable electronic transactions without physical cards. Fraudsters exploit these wallets to evade detection by creating multiple accounts under different identities, masking the original payment source, and requesting refunds to wallet balances instead of the original payment method, making it easier to convert funds into cash, gift cards, or resale value. In addition, fraudsters may load stolen credit, debit and gift cards onto the wallet for reuse.

mitigations.name: Identity Verification
mitigations.guidance: Verify the person’s identity matches what is on the card in the wallet.

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention
mitigations.guidance: Do not permit multiple use of the same credit, debit, or gift cards within a defined period.

detections.name: Location Attributes
detections.guidance: Identify impossible travel transactions for the same credit, debit, or gift card.

techniques.name: Cryptocurrency
techniques.description: Fraudsters in retail exploit cryptocurrency as a tool to hide their tracks and bypass traditional fraud controls. After committing fraud or policy abuse, they often convert refunds or store credits into crypto through gift cards, prepaid instruments, or resale of goods on secondary markets. Crypto’s anonymity, lack of centralized oversight, and irreversible transactions make it ideal for laundering value obtained from fraudulent returns. Fraudsters also use multiple wallets, peer-to-peer exchanges, and privacy coins to fragment and obscure transaction history. This enables them to quickly move value across borders and outside retailer monitoring systems, making detection and recovery extremely difficult.

mitigations.name: Identity Verification
mitigations.guidance: Positively verify the identity of the customer.

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention
mitigations.guidance: Do not accept Cryptocurrency in your marketplace.

detections.name: Transaction data
detections.guidance: Use CTI to correlate and identify crypto wallets that are either suspicious or have been identified as supporting illegal activity or fraud.

techniques.name: Gift Cards as Defense Evasion
techniques.description: Commonly exploited in fraud schemes due to their anonymity, liquidity, and ease of transfer. Fraudsters use them to bypass traditional detection systems by converting stolen funds or merchandise into gift card balances, which are harder to trace.

mitigations.name: Primary Gift Card Lock in
mitigations.guidance: For gift cards, lock the gift card into the identity of the purchaser. Do not allow another person to use the gift card without identity verification or authentication.

mitigations.name: Login Required
mitigations.guidance: For gift cards, require an account before permitting purchase of or transfer.

detections.name: Transaction Data
detections.guidance: Identify suspicious purchases of commonly resold items with potentially illicitly obtained gift cards.

references: Detecting and Reporting the Illicit Financial Flows Tied to Organized Theft Groups (OTG) and Organized Retail Crime (ORC)

mitigations.name: Primary Gift Card Lock In
mitigations.description: Ensure the purchaser is the only person that can monetize the gift card.

mitigations.name: Login Required
mitigations.description: Ensure a resource is tied to an authentication source before allowing activation, use or transfer.

mitigations.name: Access Code Required
mitigations.description: Require an access code before permitting access to a resource.

mitigations.name: Multi-Factor Authentication
mitigations.description: This involves requiring two forms of identification, such as a password and a fingerprint or a password and a one-time code sent to a mobile device.

mitigations.name: Anti-Theft Prevention
mitigations.description: Additional physical protection of products from theft (e.g. locked shelving, containers, vending machines, storing items behind checkout counter, etc.).

mitigations.name: Training and Awareness
mitigations.description: The fraudster uses digital resources to convert illicit resources into liquid funds.

mitigations.name: Website Takedown Requests
mitigations.description: A formal request to a website owner, service provider, or domain registrar to remove an offending website.

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention
mitigations.description: Use capabilities to prevent suspicious behavior patterns from occurring on various systems.

mitigations.name: Restocking Fees
mitigations.description: Impose a fee for product returns.

mitigations.name: Delayed Reimbursement
mitigations.description: Delay return reimbursement for a predetermined amount of time.

mitigations.name: Brute Force Resistant Gift Card Numbers
mitigations.description: Using algorithms to generate long and complicated gift card numbers that are resistant to prediction.

mitigations.name: Gift Card Purchase Limit
mitigations.description: Enforce limits of quantity and/or the value that may be purchased by an interaction or person.

mitigations.name: DNS Registration
mitigations.description: Identify potential URLs that may be used to fool individuals and register them to your organization.

mitigations.name: Password Policy
mitigations.description: Enforce strong passwords with length and complexity requirements.

mitigations.name: Return Limit
mitigations.description: Do not allow returns over a specified amount.

mitigations.name: Security Guard
mitigations.description: A person charged with safeguarding the premises, protecting assets, preventing theft, and ensuring the safety of both customers and staff. Their duties typically include monitoring surveillance equipment, patrolling the retail space, managing access points, responding to emergencies, and sometimes assisting in loss prevention strategies. Security guards help deter shoplifting and vandalism, maintain order within the store, and contribute to creating a secure shopping environment. They may also be involved in checking receipts, managing crowd control during peak times or special events, and coordinating with law enforcement when necessary.

mitigations.name: Satchel Control
mitigations.description: Control the admittance or size of satchels allowed at the location.

mitigations.name: Software Configuration
mitigations.description: Harden devices with configurations that can mitigate techniques or harden attack surface.

mitigations.name: Neutral Feedback
mitigations.description:
Adversaries will use return codes from public applications to gather information. When providing automatic feedback for failed requests such as accounts, gift cards, password resets, etc., provide an abstract response that does not confirm or deny that the resource exists.
For Example, if a user requests a password reset, instead of stating that the account exists and an email was sent to the email address on file, instead return “If the account exists, an email will be sent to the address on file.”

mitigations.name: Customer Notification
mitigations.description:
Send a notification to the original contacts listed on an account or resource when changes are made to the account or resources.
For example, if an address is updated for an account, send an update notification to the email and phone number listed for the resource.

mitigations.name: Identity Verification
mitigations.description: Positively verify identity of customer with government or store credentials.

mitigations.name: Escalation
mitigations.description: Require additional Escalation to manager for suspicious cases or based on dollar amount.

mitigations.name: Proof Of Purchase
mitigations.description: Require receipts and ID for high-value returns.

mitigations.name: Delivery Confirmation
mitigations.description: Only refund after the item is received and verified.

mitigations.name: Proof Of Damage
mitigations.description:
Require customers to submit photos or video evidence of damage.
Require the physical return of damaged goods before issuing a refund.

mitigations.name: Enhanced Packaging
mitigations.description:
Isolate items that could leak or cause contamination into separate packages.
Use waterproof packaging or tamper-proof seals.

mitigations.name: Redemption Limits
mitigations.description: Limit the amount of store credit that can be used on a single transaction.

mitigations.name: Law Enforcement
mitigations.description: Report known counterfeiters or other confirmed illegal activity to Law Enforcement for action.

mitigations.name: Online Location Data
mitigations.description: Restrict or block return, balance-check, and verification functions based on the originating location. Certain physical or digital locations should not have access to these functions, and locations associated with repeated fraud activity can be blocked.

mitigations.name: Phone Number
mitigations.description: Automatically block or flag phone numbers associated with VOIP services or with known fraud activity from accessing balance-check, verification, or account-recovery functions.

mitigations.name: Blacklist Known High-Risk Addresses
mitigations.description: Maintain and enforce a blacklist of shipping and billing addresses associated with prior fraud, freight forwarders, or reshipping operations, and block, hold, or flag orders directed to them.

mitigations.name: Require Signature on Delivery
mitigations.description: Require signature confirmation at delivery for high-value or high-risk orders to establish proof of receipt and reduce fraudulent non-delivery and item-not-received claims.

detection_sources.name: Anti-Theft Security Tags
detection_sources.description: A tag or similar device that is attached to an item that will cause an alarm or otherwise alert security personnel when it is removed without authorization.

detection_sources.name: Video Surveillance Systems
detection_sources.description: Cameras and related equipment used for monitoring activities in various settings to enhance security, deter crime, and gather evidence when necessary.

detection_sources.name: Behavioral Attributes
detection_sources.description: Information involving user's behavior and habits. For example, a system might use a user's typing pattern, mouse movements, preferred language, or how they navigate an application, etc., to look for deviations from normal or compare similarity to known abuse or fraud patterns.

detection_sources.name: Time-Based Attributes
detection_sources.description: Time an action occurred that can be compared against a baseline of activity.

detection_sources.name: Device Attributes
detection_sources.description: Data related to a user's device, such as a smartphone or laptop, as indicators that identify what type of device and software they are using. For example, a system might require a specific cookie or device identifier, expect a consistent device profile to include screen resolution, memory, operating system, time zone, installed plug-ins or other data that may be used to measure device similarity.

detection_sources.name: Velocity Attributes
detection_sources.description: Frequency or unusual velocity of an action compared to baseline by some aggregation value. An action might be gift card balance checks. An aggregation value might be a device identifier, IP address, user account ID, or other value. Optionally there can be a metric aggregation like count, sum, distinct count, average, standard deviation, etc. A concrete example might be looking for a large volume of orders in a short period of time for an account.

detection_sources.name: Network Traffic Attributes
detection_sources.description: Metadata about an IP address like whether it is a hosting provider, VPN or Proxy service, Residential network, cellular provider, or residential ISP. This information may also be associated with user accounts or devices to baseline them over time and look for deviations from the usual access patterns.

detection_sources.name: VOIP Attribute
detection_sources.description: A VOIP (Voice over Internet Protocol) number is a virtual phone number that is not tied to physical telephones or mobile phones. These numbers are highly portable and may be swapped and reused.

detection_sources.name: Online Identities
detection_sources.description: Email addresses, Telegram usernames, social media handles, accounts, etc., that have been the source of fraudulent activities.

detection_sources.name: Transaction Data
detection_sources.description: Records that are related to transactions in-store or online.

detection_sources.name: Market Resale Data
detection_sources.description: Monitor sales of items through third-party market monitoring and other resale data.

detection_sources.name: Controlled Purchase
detection_sources.description: Purchase items from Third Party Supplier to identify indicators of fraud.

detection_sources.name: Item Condition & Tag Checks
detection_sources.description:
Ensure item is returned with all its components such as packaging, accessories, and documentation in good condition.
Verify additional attributes such as weight, general wear and tear.
